questions.name: is_datapoint
questions.instructions: Does the segment contain a concrete, quantifiable or checkable fact (a specific number, date, name, measurement or event that could be verified)?

criteria.yes: It states at least one specific, checkable fact such as a number, date, amount, measurement or named event.
criteria.no: It is general, vague, rhetorical or purely descriptive, with nothing concrete to check.
criteria.unknown: The text is too fragmentary or ambiguous to judge.

questions.name: kind
questions.instructions: Which kind of statement is this segment?

criteria.stat: A statistic or numerical measurement: an explicit quantity, rate, percentage, amount, or count.
criteria.timeline_event: Describes a historical occurrence, plot development, action taken, mission, or specific event tied to an era, sequence, or explicit timeframe.
criteria.comparison: Explicitly contrasts, balances, or links two or more distinct entities, configurations, or operational before-and-after states.
criteria.quote: Reported speech, verbatim testimonies, or direct quotations explicitly attributed to a source or person.
criteria.definition: Strictly explains the core meaning, translation, structure, or scope of an abstract concept, technical term, code project, or acronym.
criteria.list: An explicit enumeration, series of items, or consecutive steps detailed sequentially.
criteria.claim: An abstract assertion, strategic argument, hypothesis, or speculative opinion that lacks direct empirical data or confirmation.
criteria.narrative: Storytelling, scene-setting, or background prose tracking psychological reactions, states of being, or environment descriptions without fresh actions.
criteria.other: None of the above descriptions fit.

questions.name: importance
questions.instructions: How important is this segment for someone skimming the document for its key points?
criteria: Trivial: filler, transitions or minor detail.
Critical: a headline finding or central fact.
